population: Freeze all nonzero question/contrast credits in the physically resolved verified-cases receipt, retaining repeated questions under different backgrounds. Prioritize contrasts with collateral rank changes, then preserve original registered order. The grouped physical results were known when this finer study was designed.
treatment: For every direct changed rank, separately substitute the loser's text at that one rank in the winning ordered reader prompt and the winner's text at that rank in the losing prompt. Keep the remaining ranks in their original order and allow identical texts at different ranks. Recompute both original prompts and reproduce their physical requests, raw answers, tokens and original F1; score new greedy reader calls under the original panel backend. Record the incoming and outgoing text, their actual last write, and whether the replacement text is from the focal span and absent from the opposite immediate bank.
interpretation: Mark a rank necessary in the winning background only if its replacement removes the complete reference with lower F1 under the established strict recovery rule; mark sufficient in the losing background when a single transplanted rank restores the reference with higher F1. Report these separately and retain all negative results and test counts. This single-rank intervention does not identify individual text semantics or establish policy performance. It cannot create selection credit; a later experiment may use necessary or sufficient actual source passages as training cues with target-history exclusion. Target QA or final memory reads must never enter a deployment actor.
